comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RCA/design escalation (2026-08-17), before implementation. The inert manual result is confirmed: review_code() checks code_review_enabled(repo_root) before building a request, so explicit CLI/library/MCP intent is discarded when verify.enable_code_review is false. Caller inventory found exactly two production paths: the public shim and review_bot/adapter.py. The adapter intentionally sends enabled=True because deployed receiver activation is already the enforcement decision; rebar.toml currently sets no enable_code_review key, yet Gerrit LLM-Review is live. Therefore renaming the flag to enforce_code_review and removing the adapter override would disable the live Gerrit gate unless an operational config/deployment migration lands atomically.

Decision required. Recommended compatible contract: explicit public review-code always runs (the shim sends enabled=True); preserve verify.enable_code_review as the opt-in default only for direct/internal produce_code_review_verdict calls; keep the review-bot explicit override because receiver deployment is its enforcement control; update docs to stop describing explicit review-code as disabled. Alternative: create a true enforce_code_review key, wire the voter to it, and coordinate repo/deployment config so Gerrit remains enforced; this is a broader operational semantic change. No production edit or reproduction gate has started pending operator choice.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATOR RULING (recorded verbatim, attributed to the operator): "review-code should not require a config key to be active. It should operate comparably to plan review: a config key controls whether it is REQUIRED, not whether it is AVAILABLE. Making it required is out of scope for this bug; dropping the config key gating availability is approved." — Proceeding under this ruling: only the explicit CLI/library/MCP review-code surface loses the availability gate; gate-triggered/automatic call sites keep their current enablement behavior; no enforcement semantics are added.

Phase 1 root cause (cited): shim.py review_code() gated on gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled() (verify.enable_code_review, default False) and returned _disabled_review_result() — so the explicit CLI/library/MCP surface was silently inert. Caller inventory (Serena find_referencing_symbols + grep-as-string): code_review_enabled has exactly two prod callers (the shim + the enabled=None fallback in _code_review_preflight); shim.review_code is reached only from explicit surfaces (CLI _llm_commands.py, MCP _mcp_llm.py, library export); produce_code_review_verdict's only other direct caller is review_bot/adapter.py (already enabled=True).

Fix (per operator ruling, mirroring review-plan's availability-vs-requiredness shape): the shim now always dispatches the gate with enabled=True — an explicit invocation is the caller's intent. verify.enable_code_review keeps its exact current meaning for dispatch-level callers that leave enabled=None (automated paths unchanged; no enforcement added — out of scope). _disabled_review_result and the CLI's dead code-review-disabled exit branch removed. Without the [agents] extra, an explicit run now degrades honestly to INDETERMINATE (library: no raise; CLI: exit 2) instead of a PASS-looking empty result — verified by simulation. RED→GREEN: new test test_review_code_runs_gate_even_when_config_key_is_off seen failing on the old code, green after the fix; disabled-behavior tests repointed at the dispatch level. Docs updated (passing-code-review guide, llm-framework.md, _config_schema comment, package docstrings). make lint, mypy (619 files), complexity ratchet (new=0 increased=0, stale=1 = sanctioned improvement), 200 targeted tests pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`verify.enable_code_review` (default False — src/rebar/_config_schema.py:191, parsed in src/rebar/_config_sections.py:26) is wired as an ENABLEMENT switch for the whole code-review capability, not an ENFORCEMENT switch for the gate. `gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled()` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:273) is consulted at the top of `rebar.llm.code_review.shim.review_code()` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py:168), and when the flag is off a MANUAL, explicit invocation — the CLI `rebar review-code`, the library `review_code()`, the MCP `review_code` tool — does zero work and returns the inert `_disabled_review_result()` ("code-review capability disabled (verify.enable_code_review is off).", empty findings, UNPINNED provenance).

Why this is wrong:
- An explicit manual invocation IS the operator's statement of intent. Gating it on a config var conflates two different questions: "should code review run when asked?" (always yes — the user asked) and "should code review be ENFORCED as a blocking gate in automated flows?" (the thing a config knob should decide).
- AGENTS.md and `rebar explain review` tell authors to "preview the review locally with `rebar review-code` before you push". On any checkout that has not flipped `verify.enable_code_review`, that documented flow silently returns an empty PASS-looking verdict — a trap: the author believes their change was reviewed clean when nothing ran.
- The workaround inside rebar itself proves the design smell: the review-bot adapter must FORCE-ENABLE the capability to do its job (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:16, `request.enabled` override at gate_dispatch.py:373).
- Sibling gates already model this correctly: the criteria-registry posture distinguishes per-criterion `blocking_enabled` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:62) — i.e., enforcement — from the operation being invocable at all.

## Approach (direction, refine at claim time)
Repurpose the config axis from enablement to enforcement:
- A manual/explicit `review-code` invocation (CLI, library, MCP) always runs the four-pass gate — no config precondition beyond a working LLM config.
- The config knob (renamed or reinterpreted, e.g. `verify.enforce_code_review` / gate-posture semantics) decides only whether automated flows treat code-review as a required/blocking gate (voter posture, workflow dispatch), preserving today's off-by-default ENFORCEMENT.
- Keep the inert-empty-result shape for automated dispatch paths when enforcement is off, so existing pipelines that probe the gate cheaply do not start paying LLM costs.
- Decide the compatibility story for the existing `verify.enable_code_review` key explicitly (tombstone-warn or alias), matching the deprecation conventions used for prior config-key removals.

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py — drop the enabled() precondition from the manual entrypoint
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py — split enforcement posture from invocability
- src/rebar/_config_schema.py — enforcement-semantics key (+ compat handling for enable_code_review)
- src/rebar/_config_sections.py — parse the new/renamed key
- src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py — remove the force-enable workaround
- docs/config.md — document enforcement semantics

## Scope narrowed by operator ruling (2026-08-21, recorded in comments)
"review-code should not require a config key to be active. It should operate comparably to plan review: a config key controls whether it is REQUIRED, not whether it is AVAILABLE. Making it required is out of scope for this bug; dropping the config key gating availability is approved." The enforcement-repurposing items below are therefore struck from this bug's scope; only the availability-gate removal lands here (Gerrit change 2010, commit a1a6a151bc).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar review-code` on a checkout with no code-review config key set runs the four-pass gate and returns real findings (not the inert "capability disabled" result).
- [x] The library `review_code()` and MCP `review_code` tool behave identically to the CLI in that respect.
- [x] A config knob still exists that controls whether AUTOMATED dispatch runs the code-review gate, default off, and automated dispatch honors it: `verify.enable_code_review` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py) is consulted by `_code_review_preflight` when a `CodeReviewRequest` leaves `enabled=None` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py), pinned by tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py::test_produce_verdict_disabled_is_inert_and_makes_zero_llm_calls and tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py::test_disabled_code_review_never_invokes_runner. (Per the operator ruling, REPURPOSING it into a blocking-enforcement knob is out of scope for this bug.)
- [x] The review-bot adapter (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py) keeps its explicit `enabled=True` — per the operator ruling and the 2026-08-17 escalation comment, receiver deployment is its enforcement control — and its module docstring now documents that this is the same intent-is-authoritative semantics as the explicit surface, not a workaround.
- [x] The `verify.enable_code_review` key is neither renamed nor deprecated (struck per the operator ruling — no compatibility disposition is needed): it keeps its current meaning for `enabled=None` dispatch callers, documented at its declaration in src/rebar/_config_schema.py and in `code_review_enabled`'s docstring (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py).
- [x] The `rebar explain review` guide and llm-framework/config docs describe the availability semantics (explicit invocation always runs; the key gates only `enabled=None` dispatch). docs/config.md carries no entry for this key; the generated docs/config-reference.md row remains accurate unchanged.
